extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and community stakeholders who want to participate in federal NEPA reviews / submit NEPA comments
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for citizens on when and how to participate in NEPA reviews and what makes an effective, substantive public comment on federal environmental reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Categorical Exclusion (CE)
rubrics_metrics.description: Routine actions not requiring full review
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used for routine actions that the agency has determined do not individually or cumulatively have a significant effect on the environment; no EA or EIS required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Assessment (EA)
rubrics_metrics.description: Brief assessment determining whether full EIS needed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An EA is a concise public document that provides evidence and analysis for determining whether to prepare an EIS or issue a Finding of No Significant Impact (FONSI).

rubrics_metrics.name: Environmental Impact Statement (EIS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comprehensive review for major federal actions with significant environmental impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An EIS provides a full analysis of environmental impacts, reasonable alternatives, and mitigation measures for major federal actions expected to have significant effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoping (Earliest)
rubrics_metrics.description: Notice of Intent published in Federal Register; public meetings and written comment opportunities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scoping is the stage with the most influence: it shapes what alternatives and impacts are studied. Submit comments early to influence the scope and range of alternatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Draft EIS (Substantive)
rubrics_metrics.description: Minimum 45-day comment period; comments inform Final EIS; agency must respond to substantive comments
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the draft EIS comment period to provide substantive input—agencies must consider and respond to substantive comments in the Final EIS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final EIS (Limited)
rubrics_metrics.description: 30-day waiting period before Record of Decision; comments can be received but typically less impact
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments at this stage are generally less influential on content, but the 30-day waiting period allows for review before the Record of Decision is signed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record of Decision (Implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Documents the chosen alternative; comments at this stage are typically procedural
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The ROD documents the selected course of action and implementation. Post-ROD comments are usually limited to procedural or implementation concerns rather than substantive changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be specific about the impact you're concerned about
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify precisely what environmental impact you are addressing
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid vague statements of concern; describe the particular effect (e.g., water quality degradation, habitat loss) and where/how it occurs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify affected resources (physical, biological, social, economic, cultural)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specify which resources are affected by the proposed action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List and describe the relevant resources (e.g., wetlands, species, community health, cultural sites) so the agency can connect your concern to the analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suggest specific alternatives
rubrics_metrics.description: Propose concrete alternatives to the agency's proposed action
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Well-developed, reasonable alternatives that differ from those analyzed can prompt additional study; explain how your alternative reduces impacts or meets project goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offer mitigation measures
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommend measures to avoid, minimize, or mitigate impacts
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe practicable mitigation (timing, design changes, monitoring) and, if possible, provide supporting evidence that mitigation would be effective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant data, studies, or local knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Support comments with factual information or documentation
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach or cite studies, monitoring data, maps, photos, or firsthand local knowledge to bolster claims of impacts or necessary analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify procedural concerns (notice, comment opportunity, etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: Point out deficiencies in the NEPA process or opportunities missed
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Raise issues such as inadequate public notice, insufficient comment periods, or failure to consider required actions; procedural objections can affect the validity of the review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cite EJSCREEN or other environmental data tools
rubrics_metrics.description: Use available environmental justice and data tools to support your comment
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Referencing recognized data sources (e.g., EJSCREEN) can strengthen claims about disproportionate impacts and help quantify environmental justice concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address cumulative impacts
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider the project’s impacts together with other past, present, and reasonably foreseeable future actions
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how the action combines with other projects to create greater impacts than analyzed in isolation; provide examples or data where possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment: questions the accuracy of information (with reasonable basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Challenge factual statements or data in the EIS when you have a reasonable basis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Point to contradictory data, errors, missing context, or outdated studies and supply evidence or sources to support your challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment: questions adequacy of methodology (with reasonable basis)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argue that analytical methods or assumptions are inadequate or inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain why a methodology is flawed (e.g., improper modeling, insufficient sampling) and suggest better approaches or standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment: presents new information relevant to analysis
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide information not previously considered by the agency that bears on the environmental analysis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit new studies, observations, or data that fill analytical gaps; clearly explain relevance to the issues and impacts being analyzed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment: presents reasonable alternatives that vary from those analyzed
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer alternatives that differ meaningfully from the agency’s analyzed range
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alternatives should be plausible, implementable, and tied to reducing impacts or meeting the project purpose; explain feasibility and expected outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substantive comment: causes changes or revisions in the proposal
rubrics_metrics.description: A comment that results in changes to the proposal or analysis is substantive
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comments showing concrete ways the proposal should be revised—backed by evidence—are those agencies are required to consider and respond to.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-substantive comment: merely expresses preference (support or oppose)
rubrics_metrics.description: Comments that only state support or opposition without factual or analytical basis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pure expressions of opinion are recorded but typically do not require agency responses or changes to analyses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-substantive comment: repeats issues already addressed
rubrics_metrics.description: Reiterating points already fully considered in the document without adding new information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you raise an issue already analyzed, add new factual support or point to gaps in the existing analysis to make it substantive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-substantive comment: lacks specific factual support
rubrics_metrics.description: Assertions without data, sources, or a reasonable basis
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be substantive, back claims with evidence, examples, citations, or local knowledge; unsupported assertions are unlikely to affect agency decisions.
